items.stem: Define the term 'frame'.
items.answer: A single still image in an animation; frames shown quickly one after another create the illusion of movement.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: A single still image in an animation; frames shown quickly one after another create the illusion of movement. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between a motion tween and a shape tween.
items.answer: A motion tween moves or transforms an object (position, scale, rotation) between keyframes while keeping its shape; a shape tween morphs one shape into another.

items.stem: Explain why a higher frame rate increases the file size of an animation.

items.stem: Explain what is meant by the term 'tweening'.
items.answer: Automatically generating the in-between frames from one keyframe to the next, changing position, size, rotation, colour or shape gradually.

items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: A feature that shows faint images of the previous and next frames so the animator can position objects accurately. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'keyframe' and 'tweening'.
items.answer: keyframe: A frame in which the animator sets the position or properties of an object; frames between keyframes can be generated automatically. tweening: Automatically generating the in-between frames from one keyframe to the next, changing position, size, rotation, colour or shape gradually.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: keyframe correctly described; 1 mark: tweening correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Assertion (A): Tweening reduces the work of an animator. Reason (R): In-between frames are generated automatically from keyframes. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A is true and R explains why A is true.

items.stem: In an animation at 25 fps, a cloud has an opacity of 100% at keyframe 1 and 40% at keyframe 11, with a linear motion tween between them. Calculate the opacity at frame 8.
Students at SwiftCar Rentals in Doha are learning to produce short animations. Explain the effect of choosing a frame rate of 12 fps rather than 30 fps.
items.answer: Fewer frames: smaller file and less work, but jerkier motion.
items.markingKey: 1 mark size/work; 1 mark smoothness. [2]

items.stem: Noah is creating a 30-second animated advert for FreshFarm Foods in Muscat. (a) Explain how tweening is used. (b) Describe what onion skinning shows.
items.answer: (a) Software calculates in-between frames between two keyframes, gradually changing properties. (b) Faint images of neighbouring frames to help position objects.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each part. [2] (b) 1 mark each part. [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Define the term 'animation layer'. (b) State what is meant by 'motion path'.
items.answer: (a) A separate track on the timeline holding one object or group, so it can be animated independently of others. (b) A line or curve drawn so that an animated object follows it during a tween.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: A separate track on the timeline holding one object or group, so it can be animated independently of others. [2] (b) 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: A line or curve drawn so that an animated object follows it during a tween. [2]

items.stem: Describe the difference between 'timeline' and 'animation layer'.
items.answer: timeline: The part of animation software that shows frames in order for each layer, where keyframes and tweens are placed. animation layer: A separate track on the timeline holding one object or group, so it can be animated independently of others.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: timeline correctly described; 1 mark: animation layer correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Assertion (A): Separate layers let objects be animated independently. Reason (R): The distance moved between frames is reduced. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A and R are both true statements, but R does not explain A.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'animation layer' and 'easing'.
items.answer: animation layer: A separate track on the timeline holding one object or group, so it can be animated independently of others. easing: Changing the speed of a tween so that movement starts or ends gradually instead of at a constant speed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: animation layer correctly described; 1 mark: easing correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem:
An animation runs at 24 fps and has 144 frames. The timeline shows:
Layer "Star": visible from frame 42 to frame 105
Layer "Sun": visible from frame 56 to frame 126
Layer "Button": visible from frame 29 to frame 140
Frame 1 is shown at time 0 s. State which objects are visible at time 4.9 s.
items.answer: frame 118: Sun, Button
items.markingKey: frame = 4.9 × 24 + 1 = 118 (whole frames) [1]; visible: Sun, Button [1]. [2]

items.stem: Noah is animating a logo reveal for Silverline Couriers in Muscat. Describe how a motion path would be used.
items.answer: Draw the path; attach the object; tween follows path between keyframes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per point, max 2. [2]

items.stem: Tariq is animating a logo reveal for Pioneer Insurance in Lagos. Explain how layers would be organised.
items.answer: Background, each moving object and text on separate layers; lock/hide layers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per point, max 2. [2]

items.stem: MetroBus in Manila wants an animated banner for its website. Evaluate the use of vector animation rather than video for the web banner of MetroBus.
items.answer: Points for: small file sizes; scalable; easy to edit. Points against / limitations: less realistic; complex scenes are hard; browser support issues for some formats. Conclusion: vector animation suits logos and banners; video suits real-world footage.

Against: less realistic; complex scenes are hard; browser support issues for some formats. Conclusion may argue: vector animation suits logos and banners; video suits real-world footage. [4]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) State what is meant by 'MP4'. (b) Explain what is meant by the term 'HTML5 animation'.
items.answer: (a) A compressed video file format (usually H.264) widely supported on websites, phones and social media. (b) Animation created with HTML, CSS and JavaScript (or SVG) that runs in a web browser without plug-ins.

items.stem: Pioneer Insurance in Doha needs its animated advert in formats for its website, social media and a cinema screen. Explain why the audience's devices should be considered.
items.answer: Formats and resolutions must be supported and load quickly on phones or slow connections.

items.stem: An animated GIF is 200 × 200 pixels with 8 bits per pixel and 20 frames. Compression reduces the data to one half of its original size. Calculate the file size in KB (1 KB = 1000 bytes).
items.answer: 400 KB

items.stem: Leila is exporting a short animation made for Atlas Museum in Mexico City. Evaluate the choice of export format for the animations of Atlas Museum.
items.answer: Points for: MP4 gives quality and small size; GIF loops simply; HTML5 is interactive and scalable. Points against / limitations: one format rarely suits every platform; compression reduces quality; older devices may not support some formats. Conclusion: export several versions matched to each platform and audience.
